answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying trading rights to a continuous stream of verified useful work instead of account creation. Each agent must regularly submit proofs of completed verification tasks, and its trade quota scales with that output. A summit of idle accounts earns nothing, since standing accrues only from real work over time. A newcomer starts at the jetty, with small limits, until its record climbs the ridge of sustained honest contributions. Spinning up a thousand fakes multiplies the work burden a thousandfold, so attackers pay in compute and time per identity.
